    10	
    11	The **frozen intermediate handoff shape** of the DAT-glue node
    12	(`informal/w4-datglue-worksheet.md` §1/§3.3/§3.4; DG-0 row of §4).  The 01JJ
    13	`RepresentableBy` assembly is honest only at a *separably closed* base `K_s` (DAT-B
    14	staging finding, I-0248): the raw 01JJ output is a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor` at
    15	`K_s`, not at the challenge base `k`.  The `K_s → k'` finite-level transfer (DAT-G0, the
    16	worksheet-first mountain owned by DAT-glue; mini-spec `informal/spec-datg0.md`) lands its
    17	output in this structure — a representation at a **finite separable** `k'/k` — which is
    18	exactly the interface the downstream DAT-G lane (finite Galois / Speiser descent `k' → k`)
    19	consumes.
    20	
    21	`PicRepDatum` is deliberately the `JacobianData` shape *minus* the quasi-compactness
    22	certificate (re-derived at `k'` by the same image-of-`DivScheme` argument, or inherited
    23	a posteriori by DAT-J at `k`; worksheet §3.4) and *plus* the `[Algebra k k']` datum that
    24	records how the intermediate field sits over the challenge base.
    25	
    26	## Binder deviation from the worksheet §3.3 skeleton (RECORDED, forced by elaboration)
    27	
    28	The worksheet §3.3 froze `structure PicRepDatum (k' : Type u) … [Algebra k k'] …` with `k`
    29	an *ambient* `variable {k}`.  That does not elaborate for *consumers*: unlike
    30	`JacobianData C` (where `C : Over (Spec (.of k))` pins `k`), here the explicit data pin
    31	only `k'` (`C' : Over (Spec (.of k'))`), and `k` occurs solely inside `[Algebra k k']`, so
    32	`PicRepDatum k' C'` leaves `k` an undetermined metavariable (`Algebra ?m k'` typeclass
    33	stuck).  DG-0 therefore makes **`k` explicit** — `PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the minimal change
    34	that keeps every field, instance, and the mathematical content of the frozen shape while
    35	making `k` recoverable.  The frozen *math* (fields `J`/`rep`/`lft`, the four curve
    36	instances, `[Algebra k k']`) is unchanged.
    37	
    38	## The `pic0TypeFunctor`-vs-`JacobianData.rep` defeq note (worksheet §1.1, RECORDED)
    39	
    40	The `rep` field is typed against `(pic0TypeFunctor C').RepresentableBy J`.  Since
    41	`pic0TypeFunctor C'` is the `noncomputable abbrev`
    42	`(pic0Functor C' ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
    43	(`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`), this type is **definitionally** the `rep`-field type of
    44	`JacobianData` (`JacobianData.lean`, whose `rep` is
    45	`((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J`).  So
    46	when `k' = k`, a `PicRepDatum` (with quasi-compactness re-supplied) transports into a
    47	`JacobianData` with **no massage** — recorded machine-checked by the `example` below.
    48	This is also why DAT-glue's raw 01JJ output `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
    49	(`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`) is *directly* a `rep`-shaped datum: no `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
    50	adaptation, no ε⁺-shift at assembly time (the shift lives inside DAT-C's `chartValue`).
    51	
    52	## Main declarations
    53	
    54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum k k' C'` — the frozen `k'`-level datum: representing
    55	  object `J`, the honest `RepresentableBy` datum `rep` (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and
    56	  the locally-of-finite-type certificate `lft` (carried from `K_s` along DAT-G0, worksheet
    57	  §2.3/§3.3 step 3).
    58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property in
    59	  consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C' T`, natural against `pic0Map` (owns the
    60	  `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq once, exactly as `JacobianData.homEquiv` does).
    61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicRepDatum.uniqueUpToIso` — any two `k'`-level data have canonically
    62	  isomorphic representing objects.
    63	
    64	This file is **statements/struct only** (DG-0, launchable pre-`divRep`): no
    65	`divRep`-gated producer lives here.  The producer `picRepDatumKprime` (DG-4) and its
    66	DAT-G0 transfer (DG-3) target this frozen shape.
    67	-/

     9	/-!
    10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
    11	
    12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
    13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
    14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
    15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
    16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
    17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
    18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
    19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
    20	
    21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
    22	over a field, proper over that field.
    23	
    24	## Main definitions
    25	
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
    30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
    31	
    32	## Main theorems
    33	
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
    35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
    37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
    39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
    40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
    41	
    42	## Notes
    43	
    44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
    45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
    46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
    47	-/

    53	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
    54	
    55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    56	
    57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    58	  -- smooth curve
    59	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    60	  -- proper
    61	  [IsProper C.hom]
    62	  -- geometrically irreducible
    63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

    65	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
    66	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
    67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
    68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
    69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
    70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
    71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
    72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
    73	
    74	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
    75	
    76	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
    77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
    78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
    79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
    80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
    81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
    82	  assoc := Category.assoc

    84	-- data
    85	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
    86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
    87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
    88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
    89	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
    91	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom

    97	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=

   108	  sorry

   112	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
   113	  sorry

   120	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
   121	  sorry
   122	
   123	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
   124	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
   125	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
   126	  sorry
   127	
   128	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η`) is the
   129	neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
   130	theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   131	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   132	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
   133	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
   134	  sorry
   135	
   136	/--
   137	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
   138	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
   139	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
   140	-/
   141	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   142	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   143	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
   144	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
   145	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
   146	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
   147	  sorry
   148	
   149	/-- **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a curve goes to
   150	its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line bundles. The
   151	functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
   152	the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of `Jacobian C`. -/
   153	noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   154	    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
   155	  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
   156	  map _ := sorry
   157	  map_id := sorry
   158	  map_comp := sorry
   159	
   160	end Jacobian
   161	
   162	/-! ## Base change of fields
   163	
   164	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
   165	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
   166	compatibility of the Jacobian. -/
   167	
   168	/-- Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e. `X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`.
   169	-/
   170	noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   171	    Over (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
   172	  Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
   173	
   174	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   175	    [IsProper C.hom] : IsProper ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

    Diagnostic rule
    A theorem is endpoint progress only when it is root-reachable and consumed by the next declaration on

    inventory.




3. Binding architecture decision
3.1 Chosen route
Use the curve-specialized rank-one atlas over a separably closed field, then descend. The binding route is:

    rank-one open inside Div^g
        <-> rank-one Picard open
        -> translated open cover over k^s
        -> Pic^0 represented over k^s
        -> finite Galois descent
        -> Pic^0 represented over k




3.2 Role of the high-degree divisor lane
Complete one useful vertical arbitrary-degree representability spine, then freeze broad propagation unless a
named downstream theorem consumes it. This work remains valuable for divisor geometry, Brill-Noether
theory, projective-bundle descriptions, and a possible quotient fallback, but it should not be counted as
direct completion of the old Picard open-chart seam.

3.3 When a quotient route may be reconsidered
A large-degree Abel quotient should be reopened only after a non-circular Lean-shaped theorem contract is
written. The contract must construct a scheme quotient, prove its universal property, prove base-change
compatibility, and produce the desired map to the Picard functor without assuming Picard representability.
Merely defining equality of induced Picard class is not sufficient.


4. Definition of success
The project is complete only when the same pinned representability datum is consumed all the way to the
Jacobian witness.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GaloisDescent.GaloisQuotientOverlap
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtDescentNecessity

/-!
# Consuming the finite Galois quotient in Picard descent

This file connects the global quotient producer to the first representability
clause.  The explicit quotient and kernel-pair-cover hypotheses of
`seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_lftFree` are discharged respectively by
`HasGaloisQuotient.exists_quotient` and the Galois graph cover.
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry

universe u

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme

variable {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']

/-- Clause (1) of Picard representability after consuming the global finite
Galois quotient and its kernel-pair cover.  Compared with
`seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_lftFree`, the explicit `hq` and `hcov`
arguments are gone. -/
theorem seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree
    [FiniteDimensional k k'] [IsGalois k k']
    {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    {X' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k'))}
    (rep : (picEt (Scheme.baseChangeField C k')).RepresentableBy X')
    [(semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep).OrbitsInAffineOpen]
    (hX' : LocallyOfFiniteType X'.hom) :
    ∃ Z : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
      Nonempty ((picEt C).RepresentableBy Z) ∧
        LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom ∧ IsSeparated Z.hom := by
  obtain ⟨Y, g, hq⟩ :=
    (inferInstance : AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.HasGaloisQuotient
      (semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep)).exists_quotient
  exact seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_lftFree
    (Y := Over.mk g) rep hq
    (AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.coverSelfSection_generate_mem_etaleTopology
      (k := k) (k' := k')) hX'

end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme
